scope: Exact quotient of the frozen qualified CSR for a consistent hop-count lower bound; not a replacement routing graph or a physical delay model
binding: Run manifests hash the qualified search CSR and masks, complete native node metadata, architecture fingerprint, sources and executables. Successful independent full node/arc verification is required before the probe runner accepts the quotient.
container: Shared FPGAACCP 64-byte little-endian header, schema 0.1, architecture fingerprint and payload CRC64/ECMA-182

node_groups.bin.record: u32 group ID; 0xffffffff for statically protected nodes

reverse_offsets.bin.record: u64 index into reverse_sources; monotonic, starts at zero, ends at quotient_arc_count

reverse_sources.bin.record: u32 predecessor group; strictly increasing within each destination row, no self loops

construction.group_key: (native nodes.bin column 3, native nodes.bin column 7); every unprotected node gets exactly one group
construction.group_order: First occurrence in native node order; all equal keys share one group
construction.arcs: For every qualified native arc u->v with different group IDs, emit group(u)->group(v), deduplicate, and store its reverse index
construction.relaxations: Net-exclusive ownership and connectivity within a group are ignored only while computing the potential. Full search retains exact PIP identity and per-net permissions.

proof.full: For every native arc u->v, group(u) equals group(v) or the corresponding directed quotient edge exists. Reverse shortest-hop distance H therefore satisfies H(u)<=1+H(v), H(sink)=0, and cannot exceed a concrete path's hop count. No quotient path implies no concrete path, while a quotient path alone does not establish concrete reachability.
proof.source_radius: Stop reverse FIFO BFS when the source group is dequeued at distance D. All groups at distance <D are complete. Return min(H,D), using D for undiscovered groups. This clamping preserves consistency and zero at the sink. If the source group is unreachable, BFS exhausts and uses full distances. If source and sink share a group, D=0 yields zero guidance.
proof.search: SparseSearch::run_guided orders by (g+h,g,hops,node,parent). Potential must be fixed during a query, nonnegative, consistent, and zero at the sink. Finite priority overflow rejects; UINT64_MAX is reserved for proven unreachable states.
proof.weighted_cost_warning: A hop lower bound must not be reused unscaled for arbitrary physical/congestion costs, especially zero-cost edges. Such use requires separately proven compatible edge lower bounds.

verification: Independent verifier checks all native node group descriptors and every native arc; every quotient arc must have a native witness
Byte-oracle fixtures reject missing/invented edges, wrong or protected groups and duplicate descriptors after checksums are repaired
Potential fixture compares every source/sink pair with clamped full distances and checks every quotient edge for consistency, including unreachable and same-group cases
Guided search compared with Bellman-Ford optimum on 1500 random weighted graphs; zero guidance retains 3000 dense-oracle comparisons and legacy routing results
Emitted native paths independently resolve against original PIP records, qualified CSR and net permissions

measurement.detailed_search: Expanded native labels, offered native arcs and retained label/hash/queue bytes
measurement.preprocessing: Expanded quotient groups, visited quotient edges, retained distance/FIFO bytes; each prepare also initializes group_count distance slots, including source-radius mode
measurement.not_in_counters: Index construction/verification, hashing/loading, static index storage, distance initialization instructions, total process RSS, mutable routing state or hardware execution
measurement.comparison_limit: Full and bounded preprocessing must be counted separately; differing completion counts under a search cap do not establish equal-work speedup

remaining: Native calibrated capacities/delays and edge-aware timing
Whole-design net sharing and occupancy negotiation
Worker snapshot scaling and distributed synchronization
HBM/HLS implementation and physical board evidence
